_note: Original advanced lesson. Language-specific code appears through block variants.
title: Binary Search
summary: Search sorted data by cutting the possible range in half each time.
refresher: Binary search only works when the search space is sorted or monotonic. Keep low and high bounds, check the middle, and discard the half that cannot contain the answer.

sections.title: Keep clear bounds
sections.summary: Low and high describe the part still possible.

blocks.body: At each step, `low` and `high` mark the range where the answer may still live. The middle value lets you remove half of that range.

blocks.caption: This version returns the target index or -1 when the target is absent.

blocks.prompt: What must be true before ordinary binary search is safe?
choices: The data has exactly two values
blocks.why: Binary search discards half the data based on order, so the order must be reliable.

blocks.body: Once `mid` has been checked, keeping it inside the next range can trap the loop on the same value.

blocks.caption: After checking mid, move beyond it.

blocks.prompt: Why use `low <= high` in a closed-range binary search?
choices: A one-item range still needs to be checked
blocks.why: When low equals high, there is one candidate left and it may be the target.
